q: The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the _____ of the object.
e: The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the thermal capacity of the object. Do not trade thermal capacity for specific heat capacity or latent heat.

q: The formula for thermal capacity of an object is $C =$ _____.
e: The formula for thermal capacity of an object is C = (ΔQ)/(ΔT). (ΔT)/(ΔQ) or m c ΔT is a different relation from (ΔQ)/(ΔT).

q: In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is _____ per kelvin (J K$^{-1}$).
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is joule per kelvin (J K^-1). Calorie or watt is not this quantity.

q: The thermal capacity of an object depends on mass and a _____ of the material it is made of.
e: The thermal capacity of an object depends on mass and a type of the material it is made of. Color or shape is not this quantity.

q: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is called _____.
e: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is called molar thermal capacity. Specific heat capacity or latent heat capacity is not this quantity.

q: The formula for molar thermal capacity is $C =$ _____.
e: The formula for molar thermal capacity is C = (ΔQ)/(n ΔT). (ΔQ)/(m ΔT) or (ΔT)/(n ΔQ) is a different relation from (ΔQ)/(n ΔT).

q: SI units of the molar thermal capacity is joule per mole per _____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. SI units of the molar thermal capacity is joule per mole per kelvin. Celsius or fahrenheit is not this quantity.
